p.seg: The body is venerable, but the disposition is weak,
I have disgraced my forebears. ["besmirched" captures the liveliness of classical 汙辱 better, I think. But never mind! CH]

How could I ever again brazenly ascend the grave mounds of my parents?59 59 Wang Chong (27–97?) explains this stricture by saying that parents become ancestorsupon burial and will grieve at the sight of a descendant with an impaired and shamefulbody; hence such a person does not approach their graves (see Lunheng 68.970). [How could I have the face ever again to ascend the grave mound of my father and mother (on 清明 day, as required of any filial son)? (The author would be ashamed to face his ancestors, given his failure to fulfill the duties of a son. CH]
the defilement will only deepen! [the mire (of my moral defilement) will only have got deeper! CH]
my back breaks out in a sweat that soaks my robe.
That is why my guts churn all day long.60 60 Literally, “that is why my bowels churn nine times in one day.” [And so it is that...CH]
